# 1 Enoch Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**1** Before all of this happened, Enoch had vanished. Not one of the people on earth knew where he had gone, where he was staying, or what had become of him.

**2** He had been spending his time with the Watchers, living his days among the holy ones.

**3** I, Enoch, was there praising the Lord of majesty and the King of the ages — when suddenly the Watchers themselves called out to me. "Enoch," they said, "the scribe." They spoke to me:

**4** "Enoch, righteous scribe — go and deliver this verdict to the Watchers of heaven who abandoned their exalted home, the holy, eternal place. They have defiled themselves by sleeping with women, just like ordinary men do, and have taken wives for themselves.

**5** Tell them: You have caused immense destruction on the earth. You will have no peace, and your sin will never be forgiven. And though they may love their children,

**6** they will watch those children be murdered. They will mourn the destruction of their own offspring, and they will beg and plead for eternity — but they will never receive mercy or peace."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Chapter 12 pivots from cosmic history to personal narrative — Enoch becomes a character in his own story, summoned by the Watchers (ironically) to pronounce their doom. The dynamic rendering captures the drama of the summons (v. 3) and the cold finality of the judgment speech (vv. 5–6). The punishment of watching their children be slaughtered is presented as the most fitting torment for those who abandoned heaven for earthly desire.*
